lessons.title: Same Hot Afternoon, Different Bodies: Launching the Excretion and Homeostasis Puzzle

quiz.prompt: Learners compared tilapia from Lake Victoria with other animals in their group tables. What is the main nitrogenous waste of a freshwater fish such as tilapia?
choices: Freshwater fish do not make any nitrogenous waste
Uric acid
Ammonia
Urea
quiz.rationale: The charts show that freshwater fish excrete ammonia through the gills and in lots of dilute urine. Uric acid belongs to insects and birds, and fish do make nitrogenous waste.
quiz.placement: Observe: group comparison table of excretory structures and nitrogenous wastes (freshwater fish row)

quiz.prompt: A locust and a housefly are insects. Which structures do they use to remove nitrogenous waste from the body?
choices: Kidneys only
Lungs
Malpighian tubules
Gills with chloride cells
quiz.rationale: The reference texts list Malpighian tubules as the excretory structure of insects, and they produce uric acid. Gills with chloride cells belong to marine fish.
quiz.placement: Observe: group comparison table (insects row, excretory organ/structure column)

quiz.prompt: The white, paste-like part of a chicken's droppings is mainly which substance?
choices: Uric acid
Urea
Ammonia
Undigested food (egested waste)
quiz.rationale: Birds excrete uric acid through the kidneys as a white semi-solid paste. It is an excretory waste, not undigested food, which is egested.
quiz.placement: Observe: group comparison table (birds row) and the chicken droppings example

quiz.prompt: Groups compared animals that must save water with animals that have plenty of water. Which pair of statements matches the pattern in their tables?
choices: Animals that must save water make ammonia in lots of dilute urine, and animals with plenty of water make uric acid paste
All animals make the same waste and use the same amount of water
Animals with plenty of water make uric acid, and animals that save water make ammonia
Animals that must save water make uric acid paste using very little water, and animals with plenty of water make ammonia in dilute urine
quiz.rationale: The tables link little water availability (insects, birds) to uric acid paste with very little water used, and plenty of water (freshwater fish) to ammonia in dilute urine.
quiz.placement: Observe: guiding questions 'Which animals need to save water...?' and 'Which animals have plenty of water...?'

quiz.prompt: Which statement correctly compares the urine of freshwater fish and marine fish, as recorded in the group tables?
choices: Freshwater fish produce very little concentrated urine, while marine fish produce large amounts of dilute urine
Freshwater fish produce large amounts of dilute urine, while marine fish produce very little concentrated urine
Both produce large amounts of dilute urine
Neither freshwater fish nor marine fish produce urine
quiz.rationale: The charts show that freshwater fish such as tilapia excrete lots of dilute urine, while marine fish excrete very little concentrated urine. Fish do urinate.
quiz.placement: Explain: writing why freshwater fish excrete lots of dilute urine, using evidence from the tables

quiz.prompt: After this lesson the class has data on fish, insects and birds. Which part of the hot-afternoon puzzle is still NOT yet explained, and is marked with a question mark on the class model?
choices: Which nitrogenous waste freshwater fish such as tilapia make
Why the white part of chicken droppings is a paste and not a liquid
How a goat that has been drinking water produces concentrated urine
Which structures insects use to remove waste
quiz.rationale: The lesson names the goat's concentrated urine, the dog's panting and the lizard's basking as still unexplained. The fish, insect and bird waste data have already been studied.
quiz.placement: Model: first class model with question marks for the goat's kidney, dog's panting and lizard's basking

quiz.prompt: Learners wrote questions on sticky notes for the Driving Question Board. Which question is the best 'how or why' question for investigating the goat in the puzzle?
choices: Is a goat an animal?
What is urine?
How do goats make concentrated urine even after they drink water?
Name one animal that lives in Lake Victoria.
quiz.rationale: A good Driving Question Board question starts with how or why and comes from part of the phenomenon that is not yet explained. The other choices are recall questions or do not come from the puzzle.
quiz.placement: DQB: each learner writes 2 how/why questions on sticky notes about the phenomenon

lessons.title: Inside the Goat Kidney: Cortex, Medulla, Pelvis and Nephrons

quiz.prompt: A learner predicts that a goat's kidney is just a hollow bag that stores urine. Which action would best test this prediction?
choices: Weigh the kidney and compare it with the weight of a full bladder
Cut the kidney lengthwise and observe the inside
Look only at the colour of the outside of the kidney
Measure the length of the kidney from top to bottom
quiz.rationale: Opening the kidney lengthwise lets learners see whether it is hollow or organised into regions. This is the evidence that confirms or challenges the 'bag of urine' idea.
quiz.placement: Predict: sketching the inside of a goat's kidney and Think-Pair-Share prediction

quiz.prompt: A goat kidney is cut lengthwise. Which region is the darker outer part with a fine, grainy texture?
choices: Ureter
Cortex
Renal pelvis
Medulla
quiz.rationale: The cortex is the darker outer region and looks grainy because it contains many tiny filtering units (renal corpuscles). The medulla is paler and striped, and the pelvis is hollow.
quiz.placement: Observe: dissecting the goat kidney and identifying cortex, medulla and pelvis

quiz.prompt: At the hilum of a kidney, which pair correctly names the vessel that brings blood to the kidney and the tube that carries urine away from it?
choices: Renal vein brings blood; ureter carries urine
Renal artery brings blood; ureter carries urine
Ureter brings blood; renal artery carries urine
Renal artery brings blood; renal vein carries urine
quiz.rationale: The renal artery delivers blood to the kidney for filtering. The ureter carries urine away, and the renal vein carries blood away from the kidney.
quiz.placement: Observe: examining the external kidney (renal artery, renal vein and ureter at the hilum)

quiz.prompt: In a cut goat kidney, the funnel-shaped hollow space leads into the ureter. What is the main job of this region, the renal pelvis?
choices: It collects urine and funnels it into the ureter
It stores urine for many hours until the goat urinates
It makes urine by filtering blood
It brings blood into the kidney
quiz.rationale: The pelvis does not make urine. It collects urine from the medulla and funnels it into the ureter.
quiz.placement: Explain: correcting the misconception 'the pelvis does not make urine; it collects it'

quiz.prompt: Tiny granular dots can be seen in the cortex of a kidney with a hand lens. What is the nephron?
choices: The fatty layer that covers the outside of the kidney
The microscopic functional unit of the kidney
The funnel-shaped space where urine collects
The tube that carries urine from the kidney to the bladder
quiz.rationale: Nephrons are microscopic filtering units packed in the cortex and medulla, and each one is a functional unit of the kidney. The ureter is the tube that carries urine, and the pelvis is the funnel-shaped space.
quiz.placement: Explain: introducing the nephron chart (Bowman's capsule, glomerulus, tubule, loop of Henle, collecting duct)

quiz.prompt: A goat and a freshwater fish live in the same hot area. Which statement best links kidney structure to what each animal does with water?
choices: The goat makes concentrated urine because its pelvis makes urine, while the fish has no kidney
The goat's kidney has no medulla, so it makes dilute urine, while the fish's kidney makes concentrated urine
Both animals make the same urine because all kidneys have the same structure
The goat's kidney has a well-developed medulla that helps it make concentrated urine, while the fish's kidney mainly gets rid of excess water as dilute urine
quiz.rationale: A well-developed medulla lets the goat's kidney produce concentrated urine. The freshwater fish's kidney mainly removes excess water, so its urine is dilute.
quiz.placement: Explain: connecting kidney structure to the goat's concentrated urine and the freshwater fish's dilute urine

quiz.prompt: Which order correctly traces the path of fluid through the regions of a kidney, from where it is filtered to where it leaves?
choices: Cortex, medulla, pelvis, ureter
Medulla, cortex, ureter, pelvis
Pelvis, medulla, cortex, ureter
Cortex, pelvis, medulla, ureter
quiz.rationale: Blood is filtered in the cortex. The fluid then passes through the medulla into the pelvis and leaves through the ureter. A model of the kidney should show this order.
quiz.placement: Model: building and labelling the kidney model and checking where blood enters, where filtering happens and where urine leaves

lessons.title: Following the Fluid: How the Nephron Filters Blood and Makes Urine

quiz.prompt: Blood flows into the glomerulus in a mammalian kidney. In which part of the nephron does ultrafiltration take place?
choices: Proximal convoluted tubule, where glucose is taken back
Collecting duct, where ADH controls water movement
Loop of Henle, where the medulla is made concentrated
Glomerulus and Bowman's capsule, where fluid is pushed out of the blood
quiz.rationale: Ultrafiltration happens between the glomerulus and Bowman's capsule, where high blood pressure forces small molecules out of the blood. The other regions carry out reabsorption, concentrating or ADH-controlled water reabsorption.
quiz.placement: Clip 1: blood flow into the glomerulus and ultrafiltration into Bowman's capsule

quiz.prompt: Blood cells and large proteins are found in the blood entering the glomerulus but not in the glomerular filtrate. What is the best explanation?
choices: They are too large to pass through the filtering membrane under pressure
They are secreted into the distal tubule and leave in urine
They are broken down by ADH inside Bowman's capsule
They are filtered out first but are reabsorbed in the proximal tubule
quiz.rationale: Ultrafiltration is pressure-driven and depends on size, so only small molecules such as water, glucose, urea and salts pass into the capsule. Blood cells and large proteins stay in the blood.
quiz.placement: Teacher pauses the clip at the glomerulus: 'Why are blood cells and large proteins not in the filtrate?'

quiz.prompt: A healthy person eats ugali and their blood glucose rises. Glucose is filtered into the nephron, yet none is found in the urine. What happens to the glucose?
choices: It is carried to the bladder but is too dilute to detect
It is all reabsorbed into the blood in the proximal tubule using carrier proteins and energy
It is changed into urea in the loop of Henle
It is destroyed in Bowman's capsule before reaching the tubule
quiz.rationale: Glucose is a useful substance, so it is completely reabsorbed by carrier proteins in the proximal tubule, using energy. None is left to enter urine.
quiz.placement: 'Follow the Fluid' table: glucose after the proximal tubule (Clip 2)

quiz.prompt: In the 'Follow the Fluid' table, urea is present in the glomerular filtrate and is much more concentrated in urine. Why is urea more concentrated in urine than in the filtrate?
choices: Water is reabsorbed along the nephron, but most urea stays in the tubule
Urea is reabsorbed into the blood faster than water
ADH changes the water into urea
Extra urea is made in the collecting duct
quiz.rationale: Much of the water in the filtrate returns to the blood, but urea is mostly not reabsorbed. The same amount of urea in less water makes the urine concentrated.
quiz.placement: 'Follow the Fluid' table: comparing urea in filtrate and urine

quiz.prompt: On a hot day a goat loses water through sweating and has not drunk much. Its brain releases more ADH. What does this cause in the kidney?
choices: The proximal tubule stops reabsorbing glucose
The collecting duct reabsorbs less water, so a large volume of dilute urine is produced
The glomerulus filters more proteins into Bowman's capsule
The collecting duct reabsorbs more water, so a small volume of concentrated urine is produced
quiz.rationale: ADH makes the collecting duct reabsorb more water into the blood. This saves body water and leaves a small volume of concentrated urine.
quiz.placement: Claim-evidence-reasoning: why the goat produces concentrated urine, and linking ADH to the panting dog

quiz.prompt: A freshwater fish takes in a lot of water by osmosis through its body surface. Which description of its kidney activity fits its dilute urine?
choices: It excretes the excess water as a large volume of dilute urine
It stops filtering blood so that no water enters the nephron
It makes urine only when it is out of the water
It reabsorbs almost all the water, so the urine is concentrated
quiz.rationale: Water floods into the fish, so its kidneys must remove the excess water. The result is a large volume of dilute urine, the opposite of the goat's water-saving urine.
quiz.placement: Teacher prompt: 'Fish take in water by osmosis. What would their kidneys need to do differently?'

quiz.prompt: Which statement correctly contrasts ultrafiltration with selective reabsorption in the nephron?
choices: Ultrafiltration is pressure-driven and depends on size, while selective reabsorption returns useful substances using carrier proteins and energy
Ultrafiltration uses carrier proteins and energy, while selective reabsorption is driven by blood pressure
Ultrafiltration happens in the collecting duct, while selective reabsorption happens in the glomerulus
Both processes are driven only by blood pressure and work in the same part of the nephron
quiz.rationale: Ultrafiltration in the glomerulus is driven by high pressure and depends on molecule size. Selective reabsorption, for example of glucose in the proximal tubule, uses carrier proteins and energy to return useful substances to the blood.
quiz.placement: Revising the class model: 'Where on your model is the pressure? Where is the energy-using step?'

lessons.title: Liver and Skin: Hidden Waste Processors Behind the Hot Afternoon

quiz.prompt: Under the microscope, liver tissue shows wide, thin-walled sinusoids running between rows of hepatocytes (liver cells). What does this structure allow?
choices: Sweat to be made in the liver and carried to the skin
Blood to pass the hepatocytes, so wastes and other substances can move easily between blood and liver cells
Blood to bypass the hepatocytes so that they are protected from wastes
Urine to collect between the liver cells before it leaves the body
quiz.rationale: Wide, thin-walled sinusoids bring blood into close contact with hepatocytes, so substances such as amino acids and bilirubin can be exchanged. This links the liver's structure to its function.
quiz.placement: Station A: Liver histology (hepatocytes, sinusoids, bile canaliculi)

quiz.prompt: A section of human skin shows a coiled sweat gland surrounded by many blood capillaries. Why are the capillaries important to the sweat gland?
choices: They make urea from amino acids inside the skin
They store the sweat until the body needs it
They carry sweat directly out of the pore onto the skin surface
They bring blood to the gland, which supplies the water, salts and a little urea that make up sweat
quiz.rationale: Sweat glands take water, salts and a little urea from the blood in the surrounding capillaries. The sweat duct and pore, not the capillaries, carry sweat to the surface.
quiz.placement: Station B: Skin histology (sweat gland, sweat duct, pore, blood capillaries)

quiz.prompt: A goat eats dry grass that is rich in protein. Some amino acids are in excess of what the body needs. What happens to these excess amino acids in the liver?
choices: They are changed directly into bile and sent to the intestine
They lose their amino group in deamination, which forms ammonia and then urea
They are filtered out unchanged by the liver and stored as urine
They are changed into sweat and lost through the skin
quiz.rationale: In deamination the liver removes the amino group from excess amino acids. This forms ammonia, which is changed to less toxic urea. The blood then carries the urea to the kidneys.
quiz.placement: Station C: Function cards (deamination, bile and sweat)

quiz.prompt: Old red blood cells are broken down in the body. The pigment bilirubin from the haemoglobin is removed by the liver. Where does this bilirubin go?
choices: It goes into the blood and is removed by the kidney as urea
It is lost through the sweat glands in sweat
It is excreted in bile, which passes into the intestine and leaves with the faeces
It is stored permanently in the hepatocytes
quiz.rationale: The liver excretes bilirubin from broken-down haemoglobin in bile. Bile enters the intestine and the pigment leaves in the faeces.
quiz.placement: Part 1: concept map branch (old red blood cells, liver, bilirubin, bile, intestine, faeces)

quiz.prompt: In cirrhosis, scar tissue damages hepatocytes and reduces blood flow through the liver. Which result is expected?
choices: The kidneys start to make bilirubin to replace the liver
Less urea and less bilirubin in the blood, because the liver makes more bile
Urea and bilirubin build up in the blood, and the skin and eyes may turn yellow (jaundice)
The skin makes more sweat, which removes all the wastes
quiz.rationale: Damaged hepatocytes and poor blood flow mean the liver cannot process urea and bilirubin properly. These wastes build up in the blood and cause jaundice.
quiz.placement: Part 2: resource person talk on cirrhosis, hepatitis and fatty liver disease

quiz.prompt: On a hot afternoon, a human and a horse lose heat by sweating, while a dog pants. Which statement best explains why the dog pants?
choices: A dog has no blood capillaries near the skin
A dog pants to make more bile for digestion
A dog has few sweat glands, so it loses heat by evaporation from its tongue and mouth instead
A dog makes sweat that is only urea, which cannot cool the body
quiz.rationale: Humans and horses have many sweat glands, and evaporation of sweat cools the body. Dogs have few sweat glands, so they cool by panting, which lets water evaporate from the tongue and mouth.
quiz.placement: Think-Pair-Share: which animals rely most on the skin to lose heat

quiz.prompt: A goat's urine contains urea. Which sequence correctly shows where the urea comes from and how it leaves the body?
choices: Amino acids go to the liver, where urea is made, and then the blood carries it to the kidney, which removes it in urine
Amino acids go to the kidney, where urea is made, and then to the liver, which removes it in urine
Amino acids go to the skin, where urea is made, and then to the kidney
Haemoglobin goes to the liver, where urea is made, and then to the intestine as bile
quiz.rationale: Urea is made in the liver by deamination of excess amino acids. The blood carries it to the kidney, which only clears it from the blood into urine. The kidney does not make it.
quiz.placement: Revising the class model: arrows for amino acids to liver to urea to blood to kidney

lessons.title: Feedback Loops: How the Body Keeps Water and Blood Glucose Steady

quiz.prompt: Wanjiku runs 10 km on a hot afternoon in Kericho. She sweats a lot and drinks very little water, so her blood becomes more concentrated. What will her kidneys most likely produce?
choices: A small volume of concentrated urine, to save body water
Urine with a lot of glucose, because running uses sugar
A large volume of dilute urine, to remove the extra water
The same amount of urine as normal, because the kidney does not respond to the body's water level
quiz.rationale: Concentrated blood means the body is short of water, so more ADH is released and more water is reabsorbed. This gives a small volume of concentrated urine.
quiz.placement: Predict: Wanjiku scenario (Think-Pair-Share) prediction about urine volume and concentration

quiz.prompt: In osmoregulation, more ADH is released when the blood is too concentrated. Why does more ADH lead to less urine?
choices: ADH makes the bladder store water so it is not passed out
ADH makes the glomerulus filter less blood, so no water enters the nephron
ADH is a waste product that carries water out of the body
ADH makes the collecting ducts more permeable, so more water is reabsorbed into the blood
quiz.rationale: ADH acts on the collecting duct and makes it more permeable to water. More water returns to the blood, leaving a small volume of concentrated urine.
quiz.placement: Part A: osmoregulation flowchart (ADH, collecting duct) built from the homeostasis feedback charts

quiz.prompt: After eating a big plate of ugali, a person's blood glucose rises above its set point. Which statement correctly describes the negative feedback response?
choices: The kidney alone decides to filter out the extra glucose, and no hormone is needed
Insulin removes sugar from the body by carrying it out in the urine
Beta cells in the pancreas release insulin, so liver and muscle take up glucose and store it as glycogen, and blood glucose falls back
Alpha cells release glucagon, which makes the liver release more glucose into the blood
quiz.rationale: Negative feedback detects a change from the set point and reverses it. High glucose triggers insulin from beta cells. Insulin moves glucose into cells and stores it as glycogen, so the level returns to normal.
quiz.placement: Part B: blood glucose flowchart (high glucose after a meal → beta cells → insulin)

quiz.prompt: A runner's blood glucose falls low after a long run. Which hormone is released, and which organ responds to bring blood glucose back up?
choices: Glucagon from the beta cells; the muscles change glucose into urine
ADH from the pituitary; the collecting duct releases glucose into the blood
Glucagon from the alpha cells; the liver changes glycogen into glucose
Insulin from the alpha cells; the kidney changes glucose into glycogen
quiz.rationale: Low blood glucose makes alpha cells in the islets of Langerhans release glucagon. Glucagon makes the liver convert stored glycogen into glucose, which raises blood glucose.
quiz.placement: Part B: blood glucose flowchart (low glucose after a long run or fasting → alpha cells → glucagon → liver)

quiz.prompt: A patient in Kisumu passes up to 10 litres of very dilute urine each day and is always thirsty. Tests show normal blood glucose and no glucose in the urine. Which step in the body's control system has most likely failed?
choices: Beta cells release too little insulin
The proximal convoluted tubule cannot reabsorb glucose
Alpha cells release too much glucagon
ADH is missing, or the kidney does not respond to it, so too little water is reabsorbed
quiz.rationale: Large volumes of dilute urine with normal blood glucose point to diabetes insipidus. ADH is low or ineffective, so the collecting ducts do not reabsorb enough water.
quiz.placement: Part C: case study 2, diabetes insipidus (patient in Kisumu), marking where the loop is broken

quiz.prompt: Normally all the glucose that is filtered into a nephron is reabsorbed in the proximal convoluted tubule, so urine has no glucose. Why does glucose appear in the urine of a person with diabetes mellitus?
choices: The kidney makes glucose from water when ADH is low
Too little insulin makes blood glucose very high, so more glucose is filtered than the tubule can reabsorb
Too much ADH stops the collecting duct from reabsorbing glucose
Glucagon destroys the glucose before it reaches the nephron
quiz.rationale: In diabetes mellitus, insulin is missing or ineffective, so blood glucose stays high. The proximal convoluted tubule cannot reabsorb all the filtered glucose, so some is passed out in the urine.
quiz.placement: Explain: annotating the nephron diagram to show where glucose is reabsorbed (proximal convoluted tubule) and why glucose appears in urine in diabetes mellitus

quiz.prompt: A goat on a hot afternoon produces concentrated urine, but a freshwater fish produces large amounts of dilute urine. Which explanation is best?
choices: Both animals produce the same urine, but the fish looks like it makes more because it lives in water
The goat has a high blood sugar level, which makes its urine concentrated
The goat conserves water, with high ADH and more water reabsorbed, while the fish gains water by osmosis and must excrete the extra as dilute urine
The fish has no kidneys, so its urine is just water from its gills
quiz.rationale: The goat conserves water, so ADH is high and its urine is concentrated. Water enters the freshwater fish by osmosis, so it excretes a large volume of dilute urine.
quiz.placement: Explain: applying the reasoning to the goat and the freshwater fish (Predict-Observe-Explain written explanation)

lessons.title: Keeping Cool and Staying Warm: Thermoregulation in the Dog, the Lizard and Us

quiz.prompt: On a hot afternoon in Kericho, a dog pants rapidly with its tongue hanging out. How does panting help the dog control its body temperature?
choices: The dog sweats through its tongue, just as humans sweat through the skin
Panting warms the dog's blood so it matches the air temperature
Panting makes the dog's body produce more heat so it can adapt to the weather
Water evaporates from the tongue and airways and carries heat away from the body
quiz.rationale: Panting moves air over the wet tongue and airways. Evaporating water takes heat from the body, so the dog cools. Dogs do not sweat through the tongue.
quiz.placement: Predict: Think-Pair-Share on why the dog pants while the lizard stays still on a hot rock

quiz.prompt: Blood in a mammal becomes too hot. Which response in the skin helps to lower body temperature?
choices: Vasodilation, which brings more blood close to the skin surface so heat is lost
Vasoconstriction, which reduces blood flow near the skin surface
Shivering, which makes the muscles contract rapidly
Hair erection, which traps a layer of air next to the skin
quiz.rationale: Vasodilation widens skin arterioles so more blood flows near the surface and heat is lost. Vasoconstriction, shivering and hair erection all conserve or produce heat.
quiz.placement: Observe, Station 1: Diagrams, annotating vasodilation and vasoconstriction on the mammal skin and hypothalamus chart

quiz.prompt: A field note says: 'Agama lizard on a rock at 9 am and 11 am. At 2 pm, when the rock is very hot, it moves into the shade.' What is the best explanation for this behaviour?
choices: The lizard is lazy and rests when it is tired
The lizard produces its own heat and moves to the shade to burn it off
The lizard cannot control its temperature internally, so it moves to avoid overheating
The lizard's hypothalamus makes it sweat in the shade
quiz.rationale: The lizard is an ectotherm and depends on the environment for heat. It basks to warm up and moves into shade when it is too hot. The timing of the move is evidence against laziness.
quiz.placement: Observe, Station 3: Field observation notes on the agama lizard at 9 am, 11 am and 2 pm

quiz.prompt: Body temperature control is called a negative feedback loop. Why is it called 'negative'?
choices: The response makes the body temperature change even more in the same direction
Negative feedback is harmful to the body and must be avoided
The response reverses the change that triggered it and brings the temperature back to normal
The control centre switches off and stops responding to temperature changes
quiz.rationale: In negative feedback, the response opposes the original change. For example, sweating cools a hot body, which then removes the stimulus.
quiz.placement: Explain: building the flowchart of the negative feedback loop for body temperature

quiz.prompt: A goat is standing in the cold early morning and its body temperature begins to fall. Which set of responses helps it to conserve and produce heat?
choices: Vasoconstriction, shivering and hair erection
Vasoconstriction, panting and hair erection
Vasodilation, sweating and panting
Vasodilation, shivering and sweating
quiz.rationale: In the cold loop, vasoconstriction reduces heat loss from the skin, shivering produces heat in the muscles, and hair erection traps insulating air. Vasodilation, sweating and panting are cooling responses.
quiz.placement: Explain: the reverse loop for cold (vasoconstriction, shivering, hair erection)

quiz.prompt: Some frogs and lungfish bury themselves in mud during the long dry season at the shores of Lake Victoria and become inactive. What problem does this response (aestivation) help them survive?
choices: Too much water in their bodies
Prolonged heat and drought
Prolonged cold weather
A lack of food caused by too many predators
quiz.rationale: Aestivation is a long period of inactivity that helps an animal survive prolonged heat and drought. Hibernation is the response to prolonged cold.
quiz.placement: Explain: matching local examples (burrowing, hibernation, aestivation) to the problem each solves

quiz.prompt: A dog pants for a long time on a hot day. Besides cooling the dog, what is another effect of the panting?
choices: The dog's body stops using the hypothalamus because it is already cooling
The dog's kidneys make more dilute urine to remove the extra water
The dog loses water by evaporation, so its body must conserve water and the dog needs to drink
The dog gains water from the air it breathes in
quiz.rationale: Panting cools by evaporating water from the tongue and airways, so the dog loses body water. This links temperature control to water balance, because the kidneys must conserve water and the dog must drink.
quiz.placement: Model: adding the thermoregulation loop to the cumulative model and linking it to water balance (the dog's water cost of panting)

lessons.title: Putting It All Together: Final Explanation of How Animals Keep a Balanced Internal Environment and Remove Toxic Wastes

quiz.prompt: A goat in Kajiado is kept without water for a whole day on a hot afternoon. What is the most likely result?
choices: Its urine becomes more dilute because the kidney stops working to save energy
Its urine stays the same because goats only control water by drinking less
Its blood water level rises because the body makes extra water from urine
Its urine becomes more concentrated because ADH makes the kidney reabsorb more water
quiz.rationale: Water loss raises the concentration of the blood, so ADH is released and the kidney tubules reabsorb more water. This gives a small volume of concentrated urine and helps keep the blood water level steady.
quiz.placement: Predict: goat deprived of water for a day in Kajiado (Think-Pair-Share prediction)

quiz.prompt: Learners cut open a goat kidney and review how a nephron works. Which statement is correct?
choices: The loop of Henle collects urine and carries it to the bladder
The glomerulus reabsorbs water and the tubule filters the blood
The pelvis filters the blood and the cortex stores the urine
The glomerulus filters the blood and the tubule reabsorbs useful substances such as water
quiz.rationale: Filtration happens at the glomerulus and Bowman's capsule in the cortex. Useful substances and water are then reabsorbed along the tubule, including the loop of Henle. The pelvis only collects urine.
quiz.placement: Observe: kidney specimen Predict-Observe-Explain check (cortex, medulla, pelvis, nephron)

quiz.prompt: Which row correctly matches the animal to its main nitrogenous waste?
choices: Freshwater fish: uric acid; mammals: ammonia; insects: urea
Freshwater fish: ammonia; mammals: uric acid; insects and birds: urea
Freshwater fish: ammonia; mammals: urea; insects and birds: uric acid
Freshwater fish: urea; mammals: uric acid; birds: ammonia
quiz.rationale: Freshwater fish excrete ammonia, which is very toxic but easily diluted in plenty of water. Mammals excrete urea, and insects and birds excrete uric acid, which saves water.
quiz.placement: Observe: evidence table (Animal | Environmental challenge | Waste product | Organ or behaviour | How it keeps balance)

quiz.prompt: A tilapia from Lake Victoria produces large amounts of dilute urine. What is the best explanation?
choices: It makes dilute urine because it does not need to excrete nitrogenous wastes
Water enters its body by osmosis, so its kidneys remove the excess water as dilute urine
Its body is saltier than the lake water, so it loses water by osmosis and must make dilute urine
It drinks a lot of lake water and must remove the extra salt in urine
quiz.rationale: A freshwater fish has body fluids with more dissolved substances than the surrounding water, so water enters by osmosis. The kidney removes the excess water as large volumes of dilute urine, which also carries away wastes.
quiz.placement: Explain: Claim-Evidence-Reasoning explanation for the four animals (freshwater fish)

quiz.prompt: On a hot afternoon a dog pants with its tongue hanging out, while a lizard sits still on a warm rock. Which statement is correct?
choices: Panting and basking both make the animals produce more urine to lose heat
Panting warms the dog's body, and the lizard stays still because it makes its own body heat
Panting mainly removes nitrogenous waste from the dog, and the lizard cannot control its temperature
Panting increases evaporation to cool the dog, and the lizard controls its temperature by behaviour such as basking or moving to shade
quiz.rationale: The dog is an endotherm and loses heat as water evaporates from its tongue and mouth. The lizard is an ectotherm that regulates its temperature by behaviour, basking to warm up and moving to shade when too hot.
quiz.placement: Explain: Claim-Evidence-Reasoning explanation (panting dog and basking lizard)

quiz.prompt: After a meal rich in sugar, a person's blood glucose rises above the set point. Which sequence shows negative feedback?
choices: Insulin is released, blood glucose rises further, and the pancreas stops working
Glucagon is released, the liver releases more glucose, and blood glucose rises even further
Insulin is released, cells and the liver take up glucose, and blood glucose falls back towards the set point
The kidney makes ADH, and blood glucose returns to the set point
quiz.rationale: In negative feedback the response reverses the change. High blood glucose triggers insulin, which lowers glucose back towards the set point.
quiz.placement: Explain: concept map or flowchart of a negative feedback loop (blood sugar regulation)

quiz.prompt: A patient passes very large volumes of dilute urine because the body does not make or respond to enough ADH. What explains this?
choices: The liver produces too much urea, which pulls water into the urine
The skin reabsorbs water and stops sweating
The glomerulus filters too little blood
The kidney tubules reabsorb too little water, so more water is lost in urine
quiz.rationale: ADH makes the kidney tubules and collecting ducts reabsorb water. Without enough ADH, little water is reabsorbed and a large volume of dilute urine is passed. This is diabetes insipidus.
quiz.placement: DQB wall: 'Why do diabetics pass a lot of urine?' (diabetes insipidus and ADH)

quiz.prompt: When learners add the liver to their final model to show where wastes come from, which statement is correct?
choices: The liver makes ADH, which turns ammonia into uric acid
The liver filters blood in nephrons and forms urine
The liver makes sweat, which carries urea out through the skin only
The liver removes the amino group from excess amino acids (deamination) and forms urea, which the kidneys excrete
quiz.rationale: Deamination in the liver removes nitrogen from excess amino acids and converts it to urea. The urea is carried in the blood to the kidneys and is excreted in urine. Some also leaves in sweat.
quiz.placement: Model: Final Model (organs for excretion and wastes: liver deamination and urea formation)

quiz.prompt: Which statement best explains why excretion and homeostasis are important for the survival of body cells?
choices: Excretion adds water to cells, and homeostasis makes the external environment stable
Excretion and homeostasis are only needed when an animal is ill or in a hot place
Excretion keeps the body temperature steady, and homeostasis removes urea from the blood
Excretion removes toxic metabolic wastes from cells, and homeostasis keeps conditions such as temperature and water level steady
quiz.rationale: Metabolic wastes such as ammonia and urea are toxic if they build up. Homeostasis keeps the internal conditions steady so that cells can work and stay alive, and when either fails health suffers.
quiz.placement: End of lesson: exit ticket and summary table (why excretion and homeostasis matter)
